- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.3) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast bias by 5–10% below model output.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots downward — adjust forecast by +2–5% to avoid premature mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.0–0.3) and price is trending upward, model underestimates upside — increase forecast by 3–7% for next 3–5 days.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon — apply +3% bias to first 5–7 forecasted days.  
- When sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from -0.5 to +0.3 within 3 days), model lags — adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift by +5–10% in next 2–3 days.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, model tends to underestimate true price — apply +5–8% bias to forecast.  
- Model often overestimates volatility in sentiment-neutral periods — reduce forecast variance by 15–25% if sentiment is flat.
